summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would provide for a national plebiscite at the next federal general election, asking voters about the level and composition of migration.

Its three questions would ask about substantially reducing immigration, favouring predominantly European immigration and prohibiting further Muslim immigration, with separate results for each proposal.
The vote would use adapted referendum procedures, with voting and roll closure aligned to the election and substantive commencement dependent on funding being appropriated.
changes: A proposal would be supported if more than 50% of votes favoured it, excluding informal ballots.
Casting an informal ballot would not itself constitute an offence.
Federal parliamentarians could appoint scrutineers for voting, early voting and counting within their state or territory.
During the election period, broadcasters airing material supporting one side would have to offer the opposing side reasonable broadcast opportunities.
Broadcasters would be prohibited from airing plebiscite advertisements from the end of the preceding Wednesday until polling closed.
